chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Hammad, from a man, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When the menstruating woman has performed Tawaf, then she wishes to bid farewell to the House, let her stand at the nearest door of the doors of the Mosque and bid farewell to the House.'
And when the Mutamatti'ah (woman performing Umrah al-Mut'ah) finishes her Umrah and fears menstruation, it is permissible for her to advance the Tawaf of Hajj. This was narrated.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman who fears menstruation during Umrah al-Mut'ah regarding the order of Tawaf?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of Tawaf al-Wada' (Farewell Tawaf) for menstruating women, permitting them to perform it at the nearest door of the Masjid al-Haram rather than requiring them to wait for purity or enter the sanctuary. It also establishes the legal principle of 'Qadam al-Hajj' (advancing Hajj rituals), allowing a woman to perform Tawaf al-Hajj before her Umrah Tawaf if she fears menstruation will interrupt the sequence, thereby preserving the validity of her Hajj. This reflects the Shia emphasis on practical ease (Yusr) in ritual purity and the flexibility of Hajj rites when obstacles arise.
